related_questions.question: What is the most accurate COVID home test?

text_blocks.snippet: The accuracy of at-home COVID-19 tests can vary, but generally, they are most reliable when used by individuals with symptoms and when performed multiple times over a few days. Studies show that rapid antigen tests, like the BinaxNOW, can detect about 90% of COVID cases when used by symptomatic individuals, according to Harvard Health. When used by those without symptoms, performing serial testing (multiple tests over a few days) improves accuracy according to the FDA.

list.title: Accuracy:
list.snippet: At-home rapid antigen tests can be quite accurate when used by someone experiencing symptoms.

list.title: Example:
list.snippet: Harvard Health reports a study found that BinaxNOW tests detected nearly 90% of COVID cases when used by people with symptoms, according to the journal Microbiology Spectrum.

list.title: Serial Testing:
list.snippet: If you don't have symptoms, multiple tests performed over a few days (serial testing) is recommended to increase the chances of detecting an infection says the FDA.

list.title: Example:
list.snippet: The FDA lists several tests (like the Flowflex, Metrix, and TyFast) that are designed for serial testing of asymptomatic individuals.
Follow Instructions: Always carefully follow the instructions provided with your specific at-home test.
Expiration Dates: Check the expiration date of your test to ensure it's still valid.
Variant Information: While at-home tests are generally effective, it's a good idea to stay updated on any information regarding the performance of tests on newer variants.
